stem: The graph of the linear function \(g\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. What is the value of \(g(-3)\)?
solution: From the labeled points \((0, 1)\) and \((2, -3)\): slope \(= \frac{-3 - 1}{2 - 0} = -2\), \(y\)-intercept 1, so \(g(x) = -2x + 1\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(g(3)\); the input is \(-3\), and \(-2(-3) = 6\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This computes \(6 - 1\); the \(y\)-intercept 1 is added, giving \(6 + 1 = 7\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses a slope of \(-1\); from \((0, 1)\) to \((2, -3)\) the graph falls 4 units over 2 units, a slope of \(-2\).
explanation.D: Correct. The slope is \(\frac{-3 - 1}{2 - 0} = -2\) and the \(y\)-intercept is 1, so \(g(x) = -2x + 1\) and \(g(-3) = 6 + 1 = 7\).

verify:
x = symbols('x')
g = sympify(figure['curves'][0]['expr'])
assert all(g.subs(x, q['x']) == q['y'] for q in figure['points'])
ans = g.subs(x, -3)
assert ans == 7
assert value(choices[answer]) == ans
assert all(value(choices[k]) != ans for k in choices if k != answer)
